requirements.title: The mcpserve module
requirements.rationale: MCP serving lives in its own nested module, so the root and sandbox modules still listen on no socket.

criteria.action: declare module github.com/agent-fox-dev/agentkit-go/mcpserve and go 1.27, and directly require exactly two modules: github.com/agent-fox-dev/agentkit-go v0.0.0 (replaced => ../) and github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk at the version the root go.mod requires
criteria.contract: go mod edit -json reports that path, go 1.27, one replace of the root to "../", and a direct set of exactly those two modules, which passes validateAllowlist

setup: the root module's internal/policy test helpers (go mod edit -json, directSet, validateAllowlist, parseGoMod)
check.pseudocode: m = goModEdit('mcpserve'); assert m.Module.Path == '.../mcpserve' && m.Go == '1.27'; assert replaces == {root: '../'}; assert directSet('mcpserve') == {root, sdk}; assert version(sdk, mcpserve) == version(sdk, root); assert validateAllowlist(direct, approvedDeps+modulePaths) == nil

criteria.action: name in `go list -m all` no module path that the root module's `go list -m all` lacks, apart from github.com/agent-fox-dev/agentkit-go/mcpserve itself
criteria.contract: the set difference between the two module lists, with the mcpserve path removed, is empty

setup: go list -m all output for the root module and for mcpserve (offline)
check.pseudocode: diff = paths(mcpserve) - paths(root) - {mcpservePath}; assert diff == empty

criteria.action: hold exactly one package, mcpserve, with no main package and no cmd/ directory. Its non-test files import only the standard library, the root packages agentkit, core, mcp and wire, github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/mcp and github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/jsonrpc
criteria.contract: go list ./... in mcpserve lists one package of name mcpserve, and its non-test imports are a subset of that allowlist

setup: the mcpserve directory
check.pseudocode: pkgs = goList('./...'); assert len(pkgs)==1 && pkgs[0].Name=='mcpserve'; for imp in nonTestImports: assert imp in allowlist or isStdlib(imp)

criteria.action: build every error it returns (other than a ctx.Err() passed through) with fmt.Errorf and the prefix "mcpserve: "
criteria.contract: err.Error() starts with "mcpserve: " for every non-context error returned by New, ServeStdio and ServeLoopback

setup: a nil runner, a runner whose tool has a non-object schema, and a stdio session fed an over-limit frame
a loopback listen/random failure injected through the package's test seam
check.pseudocode: for err in [New(nil,{}), New(badSchemaRunner,{}), ServeStdio(oversizeInput), ServeLoopback(failingListen)]: assert hasPrefix(err.Error(), 'mcpserve: ')

requirements.title: New and the served tool definitions
requirements.rationale: A harness must see exactly the runner's tools, under the same names and schemas the runner validates against.

criteria.condition: New is called with a nil *agentkit.Runner
criteria.action: refuse to build a server
criteria.contract: returns (nil, error) with the message "mcpserve: Runner is nil"

setup: no runner
check.pseudocode: s, err = New(nil, Options{}); assert s == nil; assert err.Error() == 'mcpserve: Runner is nil'

criteria.condition: a client sends tools/list to a Server built by New(r, opts)
criteria.action: list exactly one tool for each tool in r.Tools(). Each listed tool has the same name and description verbatim, and an inputSchema that is JSON-equal to json.Marshal(tool.InputSchema). The tool declares no outputSchema, no annotations and no _meta
criteria.contract: the listed tools and r.Tools() are equal by count and by name. For each tool, the description is equal and the inputSchema is JSON-equal, and outputSchema, annotations and _meta are absent

setup: a real Runner over several tools with differing schemas (built-in tools and code_mode)
a Server connected to an SDK/mcp.Connect client over in-process pipes
check.pseudocode: listed = client.ListTools(); for t in r.Tools(): l = byName[t.Name]; assert l.Description==t.Description; assert jsonEqual(l.InputSchema, marshal(t.InputSchema)); assert l.OutputSchema==nil && l.Annotations==nil && l.Meta==nil

criteria.condition: a runner tool has a nil InputSchema
criteria.action: serve that tool with the input schema {"type":"object"}
criteria.contract: tools/list shows inputSchema JSON-equal to {"type":"object"} for that tool

setup: a runner with one tool whose InputSchema is nil
check.pseudocode: assert jsonEqual(list[0].InputSchema, '{"type":"object"}')

criteria.condition: a runner tool's InputSchema fails to marshal, or marshals to JSON whose top level is not an object with "type":"object"
criteria.action: refuse to build a server and register no tool with the SDK
criteria.contract: returns (nil, error). The message starts with `mcpserve: tool "<name>": input schema`, and New does not panic

setup: table of runners, each with one tool named "bad": a schema that fails to marshal, a TypeNone schema with no type, a top-level array schema, a top-level string schema
check.pseudocode: for r in cases: s, err = New(r, {}); assert s==nil; assert hasPrefix(err.Error(), 'mcpserve: tool "bad": input schema')

criteria.action: read r.Tools() exactly once and serve that snapshot unchanged for the Server's whole lifetime, with no tools/list_changed notification
criteria.contract: a later change to the slice r.Tools() returned does not change any later tools/list answer

setup: a runner stub whose Tools() returns a slice the test can mutate and counts invocations
check.pseudocode: s = New(r); r.slice[0].Description='x'; r.slice = r.slice[:0]; assert listed == original; assert r.toolsCalls == 1

criteria.action: report serverInfo name opts.Name, or "agentkit" when it is empty, and version opts.Version, or when that is empty the version of github.com/agent-fox-dev/agentkit-go/mcpserve in debug.ReadBuildInfo (the replacement's version when replaced), or "(devel)" when there is none. It passes opts.Instructions to the SDK's ServerOptions.Instructions
criteria.contract: the initialize result carries serverInfo.name, serverInfo.version and instructions as described

setup: Servers built with Options{Name:"n",Version:"v",Instructions:"i"} and with Options{}
check.pseudocode: info = client.InitializeResult(); assert info.ServerInfo.Name=='n' ...; default: assert Name=='agentkit' && Version==expectedBuildVersion()

criteria.condition: New is given a runner with zero tools
criteria.action: build a server that serves an empty tool list
criteria.contract: returns a non-nil *Server and a nil error, and tools/list returns an empty tools array

setup: a Runner over an empty toolset
check.pseudocode: s, err = New(emptyRunner, {}); assert s!=nil && err==nil; assert len(client.ListTools())==0

criteria.action: be immutable after New and serve any number of loopback endpoints and one stdio session at the same time, all over the same tool set
criteria.contract: concurrent ServeLoopback calls and a ServeStdio session on one Server list identical tools, and the race detector reports no data race

setup: one Server
stdin and stdout replaced by pipes
tests run with the race detector
check.pseudocode: parallel(listHTTP(ep1), listHTTP(ep2), listStdio()); assert all equal; run with -race

requirements.title: Calls run through the runner
requirements.rationale: Every call, direct or nested inside a code_mode script, passes the runner's pipeline and Guard, so mcpserve offers no way around policy.

criteria.condition: a client sends tools/call for a served tool
criteria.action: call r.Call(requestCtx, name, arguments) exactly once, with arguments as the request's raw JSON bytes, or empty bytes when arguments are absent. It adds no preparation, guard or validation of its own
criteria.contract: the runner observes one Call with that name and byte-identical arguments (empty when absent)

setup: a Runner whose tool records every (name, input) it receives
a connected client
check.pseudocode: client.CallRaw('t', raw); assert rec[0].input == raw; client.Call('t', nil); assert len(rec[1].input)==0; assert len(rec)==2

criteria.action: answer with content of one text item holding res.LLMText(), followed by one text item for each core.TextBlock in res.Blocks in order, and drop every other block kind. isError is !res.OK, and no structuredContent, Data, Metadata or Terminate is served
criteria.contract: CallToolResult.Content has length 1 + (number of TextBlocks), the texts appear in that order, and IsError == !res.OK

setup: a runner tool returning a generated core.ToolResult
check.pseudocode: for res in genResults(): out = callThroughMCP(res); assert texts(out) == [res.LLMText()] + [b.Text for b in res.Blocks if b is TextBlock]; assert out.IsError == !res.OK; assert out.StructuredContent==nil

criteria.condition: the runner's result is a failure (invalid_arguments, blocked_by_policy, panic, handler_error or aborted)
criteria.action: return the failure as a tool result and never as a Go error or protocol error
criteria.contract: the client receives a result with isError true whose text is the runner's envelope. For a guard block, the text carries blocked_by_policy and the guard's reason

setup: a Runner with a Guard that blocks one call with a reason
tools that trigger invalid_arguments, a panic, a handler error and an aborted result
check.pseudocode: for c in cases: res, err = client.Call(c); assert err==nil; assert res.IsError; assert contains(res.text, c.code); assert contains(blocked.text, 'blocked_by_policy') && contains(blocked.text, reason)

criteria.condition: the client cancels an in-flight request, the session ends, or the endpoint closes while a call runs
criteria.action: cancel the context passed to r.Call, which is derived from the request's context
criteria.contract: the runner's handler observes ctx.Done(), and the runner's result for that call has error code aborted

setup: a tool handler that blocks until ctx.Done() and records the context error
a connected client
check.pseudocode: cctx, cancel = WithCancel; go client.Call(cctx,'block'); waitStarted(); cancel(); assert <-handlerDone; assert recordedResult.Error=='aborted'

criteria.action: run concurrent tools/call requests concurrently, without serializing them
criteria.contract: two calls, each of which blocks until both are in flight, both complete

setup: a tool that signals arrival and blocks until two calls have arrived (with a timeout)
check.pseudocode: barrier = newBarrier(2); parallel(call('rendezvous'), call('rendezvous')); assert both OK within 5s

criteria.condition: a tools/call names a tool that is not served
criteria.action: let the SDK answer and never invoke the runner
criteria.contract: the client receives a JSON-RPC protocol error, and the runner records zero calls

setup: a Runner that counts Call invocations
check.pseudocode: _, err = client.CallRaw('nope', '{}'); assert isRPCError(err); assert runner.calls == 0

criteria.condition: AgentKit's mcp.Pool, given the endpoint URL and header Authorization: Bearer <token>, calls code_mode with a script that calls read_file
criteria.action: run the code_mode call through r.Call. The script's nested read_file call also goes through the runner and its Guard
criteria.contract: the imported result is OK and holds the file's content, and the runner's Guard observes both the code_mode call and the nested read_file call

setup: a workspace containing a file with known content, built with workspace.Open and tools.For
code_mode wrapped around the tools, and a Runner whose Guard records every call
a Server on ServeLoopback
check.pseudocode: pool.Connect({URL: ep.URL, Headers:{Authorization:'Bearer '+ep.Token}}); res = tools['agentkit__code_mode'].Handler(script); assert res.OK && contains(res.Text, content); assert guardSeen == ['code_mode','read_file']

requirements.title: ServeStdio
requirements.rationale: A harness that starts the program as a child process talks MCP on its stdio, under the same wire bounds as every other inbound frame.

criteria.condition: ServeStdio(ctx) is called
criteria.action: serve one MCP session on os.Stdin and os.Stdout through mcp.NewPipeTransport under wire.Defaults(), with the same tools as every other session of the Server
criteria.contract: a client connected over in-process io.Pipe pairs (mcp.Connect with mcp.NewPipeTransport) and a client that spawns the program through mcp.Pool with ServerConfig.Command both list and call the served tools. The child-process case may skip on Windows

setup: os.Stdin and os.Stdout replaced by pipe ends
a client using mcp.Connect with mcp.NewPipeTransport on the other ends
the test binary re-executed with a marker environment variable (plus PATH/HOME), where the marker selects a main that builds a runner and calls ServeStdio
the test skips on Windows
check.pseudocode:
go ServeStdio(ctx); c = mcp.Connect(NewPipeTransport(outR, inW, Defaults())); assert names(c.ListTools())==names(r.Tools()); assert c.CallRaw(...).OK
if os.Getenv(MARKER)!='' { serveChild() }; pool.Connect({Command: os.Args[0], Env:[MARKER+'=1', ...]}); assert tools listed; assert call OK; pool.Close(); assert childExit==0

criteria.condition: the client closes its end of the session
criteria.action: write every reply already owed, then end the session
criteria.contract: ServeStdio returns nil, and every call issued before EOF has received its reply

setup: a tool that takes a short time to answer
stdin and stdout as pipes
check.pseudocode: send(call); closeWriter(); err = <-done; assert err==nil; assert replyFrames contains id of call

criteria.condition: ctx ends while the session is open
criteria.action: close the session
criteria.contract: ServeStdio returns ctx.Err()

setup: an open session with an idle client
check.pseudocode: cancel(); assert errors.Is(<-done, context.Canceled) within 2s

criteria.condition: ServeStdio is called with a ctx that is already done
criteria.action: return without reading stdin
criteria.contract: returns ctx.Err(), and no byte of stdin is consumed

setup: os.Stdin is a file holding bytes, with a duplicated descriptor sharing its offset
ctx already cancelled
check.pseudocode: cancel(); err = ServeStdio(ctx); assert err == ctx.Err(); assert dupFd.Seek(0, Current)==0

criteria.condition: an inbound frame breaks wire.Defaults() limits, or the session ends for any reason other than client EOF or ctx
criteria.action: end the session without handing the offending frame to the SDK or the runner
criteria.contract: ServeStdio returns a non-nil error prefixed "mcpserve: ", and the runner records zero calls for that frame

setup: a Runner counting calls
stdin carrying a tools/call frame with a duplicate key (or depth over 64, or longer than 16 MiB)
check.pseudocode: write(dupKeyFrame); err = ServeStdio(ctx); assert hasPrefix(err.Error(),'mcpserve: '); assert runner.calls==0

criteria.action: close os.Stdin and leave os.Stdout open when ServeStdio returns, and write nothing to stdout except protocol frames
criteria.contract: after return, os.Stdout accepts a further write. Every line written to stdout during the session is a JSON-RPC message

setup: os.Stdin and os.Stdout replaced by os.Pipe files, with a session that lists and calls a tool then ends by client EOF
check.pseudocode: _, e = os.Stdin.Read(buf); assert errors.Is(e, os.ErrClosed); _, e = os.Stdout.Write('x'); assert e==nil; for line in captured: assert isJSONRPC(line)

requirements.title: ServeLoopback listener, authentication and body guard
requirements.rationale: The HTTP endpoint is reachable only from the same machine and only with the token. An unauthenticated peer can make the server read no body and learns nothing.

criteria.condition: ServeLoopback is called with a ctx that is already done
criteria.action: listen on nothing
criteria.contract: returns (nil, ctx.Err())

setup: a cancelled ctx, and a listen hook that fails the test if invoked
check.pseudocode: ep, err = s.ServeLoopback(cancelledCtx); assert ep==nil && err==context.Canceled; assert listenCalls==0

criteria.condition: ServeLoopback(ctx) is called with a live ctx
criteria.action: listen on TCP 127.0.0.1:0 and generate a fresh token for the call: 24 bytes from crypto/rand encoded as 48 lowercase hex characters
criteria.contract: returns &Endpoint{URL: "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp", Token: <48 chars matching ^[0-9a-f]{48}$>} and a nil error

setup: a live ctx
check.pseudocode: ep, err = ServeLoopback(ctx); assert regexp(urlRe, ep.URL) && regexp('^[0-9a-f]{48}$', ep.Token)

criteria.condition: the listen call or the random source fails
criteria.action: serve nothing and release any listener it opened
criteria.contract: returns (nil, error) with the message prefixed "mcpserve: "

setup: a test seam that makes listen fail, and another that makes the random source fail after the listener is opened
check.pseudocode: for hook in [failListen, failRand]: ep, err = ServeLoopback(ctx); assert ep==nil && hasPrefix(err.Error(),'mcpserve: '); assert connectRefused(openedAddr) for failRand

criteria.condition: a request, on any path and with any method, lacks an Authorization header exactly equal to "Bearer <token>" (compared in constant time)
criteria.action: refuse the request before reading its body and before routing it
criteria.contract: HTTP 401 with header WWW-Authenticate: Bearer and body "unauthorized". The SDK and the runner see nothing

setup: a running endpoint whose SDK handler is wrapped to detect invocation
a request body that blocks forever if read
check.pseudocode: for (path, method, hdr) in matrix: r = do(); assert r.Status==401 && r.Header['WWW-Authenticate']=='Bearer' && r.Body=='unauthorized'; assert sdkCalls==0

criteria.condition: an authorized request targets any path other than /mcp
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 404, and the SDK handler is not invoked

setup: a running endpoint
check.pseudocode: for p in ['/','/mcp/x','/health']: assert do(p, auth).Status==404; assert sdkCalls==0

criteria.condition: an authorized request to /mcp has a body longer than wire.Defaults().MaxMessageBytes
criteria.action: stop reading at the limit and refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 413, and the SDK handler is not invoked

setup: a running endpoint
a body one byte over wire.Defaults().MaxMessageBytes
check.pseudocode: r = post('/mcp', bytes(Defaults().MaxMessageBytes+1), auth); assert r.Status==413; assert sdkCalls==0

criteria.condition: an authorized request to /mcp has a body that wire.Guard(body, wire.Defaults()) rejects, for example one with a duplicate key or nesting over the depth limit
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 400, and the SDK handler is not invoked

setup: a running endpoint
bodies with a duplicate key, nesting deeper than the depth limit, and invalid JSON syntax
check.pseudocode: for b in [dupKey, deep, '{']: assert post('/mcp', b, auth).Status==400; assert sdkCalls==0

criteria.condition: an authorized request to /mcp has no body or a body that wire.Guard accepts
criteria.action: replay the body byte for byte to the SDK's NewStreamableHTTPHandler with default (stateful) options, served by an http.Server with ReadHeaderTimeout 10s and handler contexts derived from ctx
criteria.contract: an initialize POST with the token gets HTTP 200 and an Mcp-Session-Id header, and later requests in that session are served by the SDK

setup: a running endpoint
check.pseudocode: r = post('/mcp', initialize, auth); assert r.Status==200 && r.Header['Mcp-Session-Id']!=''; r2 = post('/mcp', listTools, auth+session); assert names(r2) == names(r.Tools())

requirements.title: Endpoint lifetime
requirements.rationale: A client's standalone SSE stream never ends on its own, so shutdown is bounded. Tying the endpoint to ctx stops serving even when the caller forgets Close.

criteria.condition: Endpoint.Close is called or ctx ends, whichever comes first
criteria.action: stop accepting connections, shut down gracefully for at most 2 s, then force-close every remaining connection
criteria.contract: Close returns within 3 s even when a client holds a standalone SSE stream open, and a later TCP connect to the port is refused

setup: two endpoints with a client that opened an initialize and a standalone GET SSE stream that stays open
check.pseudocode: t0=now; ep.Close(); assert now-t0 < 3s; assert dialRefused(port); cancel(); eventually(dialRefused(port2), 3s)

criteria.condition: the endpoint is force-closed and a tools/call is still in flight
criteria.action: cancel the in-flight call's context
criteria.contract: the runner's result for that call has error code aborted

setup: a tool that blocks until ctx.Done() and records the runner's result
a call in flight through the loopback endpoint
check.pseudocode: go call('block'); waitStarted(); ep.Close(); assert <-recorded.Error=='aborted'

criteria.action: be idempotent and safe to call from several goroutines at once
criteria.contract: every call returns nil, and the race detector reports no data race

setup: a live endpoint
tests run with the race detector
check.pseudocode: parallel(16, assert ep.Close()==nil); assert ep.Close()==nil

criteria.condition: Close is called on an Endpoint that ServeLoopback did not return, such as the zero value
criteria.action: do nothing
criteria.contract: returns nil without panicking

setup: var ep mcpserve.Endpoint and &mcpserve.Endpoint{URL: "x", Token: "y"}
check.pseudocode: assert (&Endpoint{}).Close()==nil

criteria.condition: ServeLoopback is called twice on one Server
criteria.action: create two independent endpoints
criteria.contract: the two endpoints have distinct ports and distinct tokens. After one is closed, the other still answers an authorized initialize with HTTP 200, and its token is refused (401) by the other endpoint while that endpoint is open

setup: one Server and two endpoints A and B
check.pseudocode: assert A.URL!=B.URL && A.Token!=B.Token; assert do(B.URL, bearer(A.Token)).Status==401; B.Close(); assert post(A.URL, init, bearer(A.Token)).Status==200

requirements.title: Harness configuration strings
requirements.rationale: A harness connects to the endpoint from the JSON these methods return, so an embedder writes no configuration by hand.

criteria.condition: ClaudeConfig(name) is called on an Endpoint
criteria.action: return the JSON {"mcpServers":{"<name>":{"type":"http","url":"<URL>","headers":{"Authorization":"Bearer <Token>"}}}}, which Claude Code's --mcp-config takes
criteria.contract: the returned string decodes to exactly that object

setup: Endpoint{URL:"http://127.0.0.1:1234/mcp", Token:"tok"}
check.pseudocode: assert jsonEqual(ep.ClaudeConfig('agentkit'), expected)

criteria.condition: PiConfig(name) is called on an Endpoint
criteria.action: return the ClaudeConfig object with "exposure":"direct" added to the server entry, which Pi's .pi/mcp.json takes
criteria.contract: the returned string decodes to the ClaudeConfig object plus exposure "direct" in the server entry

setup: Endpoint{URL, Token}
check.pseudocode: exp = decode(ClaudeConfig); exp.mcpServers.agentkit.exposure='direct'; assert decode(PiConfig)==exp

criteria.condition: ClaudeConfig or PiConfig is called with an empty name
criteria.action: use "agentkit" as the server name
criteria.contract: the only key under mcpServers is "agentkit"

setup: an Endpoint
check.pseudocode: for f in [ClaudeConfig, PiConfig]: assert keys(decode(f('')).mcpServers)==['agentkit']

criteria.action: for any non-empty name string and any URL and Token field values, build the output with encoding/json so that it is valid JSON and reflects the Endpoint's current fields
criteria.contract: json.Valid is true, decoding yields the name byte-for-byte as the only mcpServers key, and url and Authorization equal the Endpoint's URL and "Bearer "+Token at call time

setup: an Endpoint whose fields are set per generated case
check.pseudocode: for (name,url,tok) in gen(): ep=Endpoint{url,tok}; for s in [Claude(name), Pi(name)]: assert json.Valid(s); e = decode(s).mcpServers; assert keys(e)==[name]; assert e[name].url==url && e[name].headers.Authorization=='Bearer '+tok

requirements.title: Options and logging
requirements.rationale: The token is a credential, and tool arguments and outputs are workspace content, so logs carry structure and never secrets or payloads.

criteria.action: have exactly four fields, Name, Version and Instructions of type string and Logger of type *slog.Logger. A nil Logger means slog.New(slog.DiscardHandler)
criteria.contract: a Server built with Options{} serves calls and refusals without panicking and without writing to stdout or stderr

setup: reflect on mcpserve.Options
a Server built with Options{} and stdout/stderr captured
check.pseudocode: assert fieldsOf(Options)=={Name:string,Version:string,Instructions:string,Logger:*slog.Logger}; run scenario; assert stderr==''

criteria.condition: a served tools/call completes
criteria.action: emit exactly one Info record with message "tool call" and attributes tool, ok, duration, plus the error code when the result is a failure
criteria.contract: a capturing slog handler records one Info "tool call" record per call, with those attributes

setup: a capturing slog handler as Options.Logger
a tool that succeeds and a tool that fails with handler_error
check.pseudocode: recs = capture.filter(msg=='tool call'); assert len(recs)==2; assert recs[0].ok==true && !has(recs[0],'error'); assert recs[1].ok==false && recs[1].error=='handler_error'

criteria.condition: an HTTP request is refused for a missing or wrong token, an over-size body or a rejected body
criteria.action: emit exactly one Warn record carrying the peer address and the refusal reason
criteria.contract: a capturing handler records one Warn record per refusal, with a peer attribute and a reason that tells the three cases apart

setup: a capturing handler and a live endpoint
check.pseudocode: warns = capture.filter(level==Warn); assert len(warns)==3; assert distinct(reasons(warns)) and all(has(w,'peer'))

criteria.condition: a stdio session ends with a non-nil error other than ctx.Err()
criteria.action: emit exactly one Warn record for that session end
criteria.contract: a capturing handler records one Warn record when ServeStdio returns a "mcpserve: " error

setup: a capturing handler
a stdio session fed an over-limit frame
check.pseudocode: err = ServeStdio(); assert count(capture.Warn)==1; cleanRun(); assert count(capture.Warn)==1

criteria.action: for any call arguments, result text, Detail and token, emit no record whose message or attribute values contain the token, the Authorization header value, the tool arguments, the result text or the Detail
criteria.contract: none of those strings appears as a substring of the captured log output

setup: a capturing handler recording the full text of every record (message and attributes), with the bearer token known to the test
check.pseudocode: for (args, text, detail) in gen(): run scenario; out = capture.String(); for s in [token,'Bearer '+token,args,text,detail]: assert !contains(out, s)

requirements.title: Build wiring and policy gates
requirements.rationale: The new module must be built, vetted, linted and documented like every other module. The existing invariants of the root and sandbox modules must not move.

criteria.action: list mcpserve in MODULES (so test, build, vet, lint and tidy run there) and in the make doc module loop, which writes docs/generated/mcpserve/mcpserve.txt
criteria.contract: the parsed `MODULES :=` line and the `@for m in` doc loop both contain mcpserve

setup: the root Makefile
check.pseudocode: assert 'mcpserve' in parseModules(Makefile) && 'mcpserve' in parseDocLoop(Makefile); assert exists('docs/generated/mcpserve/mcpserve.txt')

criteria.action: include "mcpserve" in gateModules so that the cross-target gate (cgo off, four targets) and the host-cgo build and vet gates cover it
criteria.contract: gateModules contains "mcpserve", and the gates pass for it

setup: internal/policy gateModules
check.pseudocode: assert 'mcpserve' in gateModules; run crossTargetGate('mcpserve') == ok

criteria.action: keep its scope to non-test files of the root and sandbox modules. Its doc comment and failure message say that only nested modules (sandbox/gatewayd, mcpserve) may listen
criteria.contract: a fixture with a listener in a nested mcpserve/ directory that has its own go.mod passes. A fixture with a listener in the root fails, with a message naming both nested modules. The delivered tree passes

setup: fixtures built by module(t, files) including a nested mcpserve/go.mod
check.pseudocode: assert noListen(fixtureNestedMcpserve)==nil; err = noListen(fixtureRootListener); assert contains(err,'gatewayd') && contains(err,'mcpserve'); assert noListen(repoRoot)==nil

criteria.action: leave its go.mod, its direct set, its module graph snapshot, internal/policy/testdata and the exported-API golden unchanged
criteria.contract: TS-13-65 and TS-19-64 pass

setup: the delivered tree and git HEAD
check.pseudocode: run TestRootGraphSnapshot (TS-13-65) and TestGatewayUnchanged (TS-19-64); assert gitDiff(go.mod, internal/policy/testdata)==''

criteria.action: pass make check with GOPROXY=off in every module, mcpserve included, with mcpserve's go.sum committed
criteria.contract: TS-19-66 passes

setup: GOPROXY=off
mcpserve/go.sum committed
check.pseudocode: env GOPROXY=off make check; assert exit==0

requirements.title: examples/harness served through mcpserve
requirements.rationale: The harness is the reference embedder. It must show the short path (sandbox.Open, NewRunner, mcpserve) instead of a hand-written MCP server.

criteria.action: contain no server.go. No non-test file imports a github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk package or net, or calls a listen API. calls.go keeps the per-call log, the call and blocked counts built from the toolset's hooks, and summarize, firstLine, truncate and errShellBlocked, with unchanged behaviour
criteria.contract: a structural test finds no server.go, no SDK or net import and no listen call in non-test files, and finds those helpers declared in calls.go

setup: the examples/harness non-test sources
check.pseudocode: assert !exists('server.go'); for f in nonTest: assert no import startswith sdk or == 'net'; assert declared(calls.go) >= {summarize, firstLine, truncate, errShellBlocked}

criteria.action: serve the runner with mcpserve.New(runner, mcpserve.Options{Instructions: …}) and ServeLoopback(ctx), defer ep.Close(), and print "MCP server at <ep.URL>"
criteria.contract: the offline run's account contains "MCP server at http://127.0.0.1:"

setup: the harness run offline with the scripted harness and the local provider
check.pseudocode: out = run(offlineArgs); assert contains(out,'MCP server at http://127.0.0.1:'); assert astHasCalls(main.go, ['mcpserve.New','ServeLoopback','Close'])

criteria.action: take *mcpserve.Endpoint in runHarness and in the claude, pi and scripted runners. claude passes ep.ClaudeConfig("agentkit") to --mcp-config, pi writes ep.PiConfig("agentkit") to .pi/mcp.json, and scripted connects mcp.Pool to ep.URL with the header Authorization: Bearer <ep.Token>
criteria.contract: TestHarnessArgs passes with &mcpserve.Endpoint{}, and the claude arguments carry the ClaudeConfig string after --mcp-config

setup: &mcpserve.Endpoint{URL, Token} set for the claude case, and &mcpserve.Endpoint{} for TestHarnessArgs
check.pseudocode: args = claudeArgs(ep.ClaudeConfig('agentkit'), ...); assert args[indexOf('--mcp-config')+1]==ep.ClaudeConfig('agentkit')

criteria.action: choose the source first (sandbox.GitRepo{URL, Ref, Depth: 1} for --repo, sandbox.LocalDir{Path: dir, ExcludeGit: true} for --dir, otherwise sandbox.LocalDir{Path: sample}), then create, fill and get the proxies with exactly one sandbox.Open(ctx, p, spec, src, sandbox.ToolOptions{}) call, with defer sb.Close(ctx). It calls none of Provider.Create, Sandbox.Sync and Sandbox.Tools, and prints "filled the workspace from <the sample project | dir | repo>"
criteria.contract: a structural test counts exactly one sandbox.Open call and no Create, Sync or Tools call, and the offline account contains "filled the workspace from the sample project"

setup: the examples/harness non-test sources and an offline run
check.pseudocode: assert count(calls,'sandbox.Open')==1; assert count(calls,'.Create'|'.Sync'|'.Tools')==0; assert contains(out,'filled the workspace from the sample project')

criteria.action: use guard.Allow(allowed...) in place of guard.Restricted(guard.Options{AllowedPrograms: allowed}). In the scripted harness, use faux.ToolCall(…) and faux.Text(…) in place of faux.Turn{…} literals
criteria.contract: a structural test finds no `faux.Turn{` literal and no guard.Restricted call in non-test files

setup: the examples/harness non-test sources
check.pseudocode: assert uses('guard.Allow'); assert !contains(src,'faux.Turn{') && !uses('guard.Restricted')

criteria.action: require github.com/agent-fox-dev/agentkit-go/mcpserve v0.0.0 with replace => ../../mcpserve, and after go mod tidy no longer list github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk as a direct requirement
criteria.contract: go mod edit -json shows the mcpserve require and replace, and shows the go-sdk require only as indirect

setup: examples/harness/go.mod after go mod tidy
check.pseudocode: m = goModEdit('examples/harness'); assert req(mcpserve).Version=='v0.0.0'; assert replace(mcpserve)=='../../mcpserve'; assert req(sdk).Indirect==true

criteria.condition: the harness example runs offline with the scripted harness on the local provider
criteria.action: import the served tools over MCP, run the scripted code_mode turn through mcpserve, and finish with a pass verdict
criteria.contract: output contains "filled the workspace from the sample project", "imported 12 tools over MCP: agentkit__code_mode, agentkit__edit_file, agentkit__execute", "verdict: pass" and "Harness example completed successfully", and the process exits 0

setup: the scripted harness on the local provider, no network
check.pseudocode: out, code = run(['--harness','scripted', ...]); for s in expected: assert contains(out,s); assert code==0

execution_paths.title: A client runs a code_mode script over the loopback endpoint

steps.action: builds tools with workspace.Open and tools.For, wraps them in code_mode, creates agentkit.NewRunner with a Guard, and calls mcpserve.New(runner, Options{}) and ServeLoopback(ctx)
listens on 127.0.0.1:0 and returns an Endpoint with URL http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp and a 48-character token
connects to ep.URL with Authorization: Bearer <token>, lists the tools and calls code_mode with a script that calls read_file
checks the token, guards the body with wire.Guard, replays it to the SDK handler, and calls runner.Call for code_mode
runs code_mode through its Guard. The script's nested read_file call also passes the Guard and reads the file
returns a CallToolResult whose text is LLMText() followed by the text blocks, with isError false
calls ep.Close(), and a later connect to the port is refused

setup: a workspace from workspace.Open with a known file
tools from tools.For wrapped by code_mode, a Runner with a recording Guard, a real Server
end_state: the endpoint URL is http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp with a 48-character token
the call result is OK and holds the file content
the Guard recorded the code_mode call and the nested read_file call
after Close a TCP connect to the port is refused

execution_paths.title: A harness spawns the program and talks MCP over stdio

steps.action: spawns the program as a child process through ServerConfig.Command, with a marker variable in its environment
builds a Runner and a Server and calls ServeStdio(ctx)
serves one session on stdin and stdout through mcp.NewPipeTransport under wire.Defaults()
lists the tools and calls one. The call runs through runner.Call and returns the runner's text
closes the connection, which closes the child's stdin
writes every owed reply, and ServeStdio returns nil, so the child exits 0

setup: the test binary re-executed with a marker environment variable that builds a Runner and Server and calls ServeStdio
mcp.Pool with ServerConfig.Command (skipped on Windows)
end_state: the tools are listed and the call returns the runner's text
the child's stdin is closed by the pool and every owed reply was written

execution_paths.title: Refused and blocked requests never reach a tool

steps.action: POSTs an initialize request to ep.URL without the bearer token
answers 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer before reading the body, and logs one Warn record with the peer and no header value
connects with the token and calls execute with a program the runner's Guard does not allow
blocks the call and returns a blocked_by_policy result with the guard's reason
returns the block as a tool result with isError true and the envelope text, not as a protocol error, and logs one Info "tool call" record with ok=false

setup: a live endpoint over a Runner whose Guard allows only some programs
a capturing slog handler as Logger
end_state: the unauthenticated request gets 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer and a Warn record with the peer and no header value is logged
the execute call returns a result with isError true whose text carries blocked_by_policy and the guard's reason, not a protocol error
one Info "tool call" record with ok=false is logged

execution_paths.title: The harness example runs offline end to end through mcpserve

steps.action: runs the examples/harness program offline with the scripted harness and the local provider
chooses the sample LocalDir source, calls sandbox.Open once, and prints "filled the workspace from the sample project"
builds a Runner over code_mode and the proxies with guard.Allow, then serves it with mcpserve.New and ServeLoopback and prints "MCP server at http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp"
connects mcp.Pool to ep.URL with the bearer token, imports 12 tools, and drives faux.ToolCall and faux.Text turns that call agentkit__code_mode
runs each call through runner.Call over the sandbox proxies
runs the checks, prints "verdict: pass" and "Harness example completed successfully", and closes the endpoint and the sandbox

real_components: faux provider with faux.ToolCall and faux.Text
setup: the examples/harness program built with the scripted harness and the local provider
no network access
end_state: it prints "filled the workspace from the sample project" and "MCP server at http://127.0.0.1:"
the scripted harness imports 12 tools over MCP and its faux code_mode turn runs through the runner over the sandbox proxies
it prints "verdict: pass" and "Harness example completed successfully"
the process exits 0 and the endpoint and sandbox are closed

symbols.name: NewServer
symbols.notes: Signature taken from call sites in examples/harness/server.go and examples/codemode/main.go. opts may be nil.

symbols.notes: Only the Instructions field is used.

symbols.name: (*Server).AddTool
symbols.notes: Unverified: that it panics on a missing or non-object InputSchema and does not validate arguments. New pre-checks schemas so that it never relies on this.

symbols.name: Tool
symbols.signature: type Tool struct { Name, Description string; InputSchema any; ... }

symbols.name: CallToolResult
symbols.signature: type CallToolResult struct { Content []Content; IsError bool; ... }
symbols.notes: Content holds &TextContent{Text} items. req.Params.Arguments is assignable to json.RawMessage.

symbols.name: NewStreamableHTTPHandler
symbols.notes: Called with nil opts, which gives stateful sessions. The result implements http.Handler.

symbols.name: (*Server).Run
symbols.signature: func (s *Server) Run(ctx context.Context, t Transport) error
symbols.notes: Unverified: what it returns on a clean EOF and on a Read error. ServeStdio normalizes the result itself, for example by wrapping the Connection to record the first Read error.

symbols.name: Connection
symbols.signature: type Connection interface { Read(context.Context) (jsonrpc.Message, error); Write(context.Context, jsonrpc.Message) error; Close() error; SessionID() string }
